title: Emergency contacts: data model and opt-out
subtitle: The server sends no message. The opt-out token travels in the URL fragment, which a browser never sends to a server, and then in a request body (P013a, ADR 0024)

nodes.label: App: POST /v1/contacts with name and phone in the body
App: POST /v1/contacts/{id}/invite, gets the token once, keeps it in memory only
User sends the invite from their own SMS app: link = API address + /c#token
Create: lock the user's row, sos_alerts granted? own number? duplicate? opted out? at most 5
Invite: 128 random bits, store SHA-256 only, at most 10 links per contact
GET /c: one static page for everyone, strict CSP by hash, no cookie. The request carries NO token
POST /v1/public/contacts/opt-out with the token in the BODY: shared rate limit, lookup by hash, same 404 for every bad token
Withdrawing sos_alerts deletes every contact, tombstone and token in one transaction
emergency_contacts: user_id, name, phone_e164, invited_at, opted_out_at, deleted_at. UNIQUE (user_id, phone_e164)
contact_optout_tokens: token_hash (primary key), contact_id. Never a plaintext token
opted_out_at set: never alerted, never invited again. Removed by the user: the number stays as a tombstone
Contact opens the link. Browser asks for /c only: the fragment stays on the phone
Page script reads the token from the fragment and removes it from the address bar
Contact taps Opt out. Opening the link alone changes nothing
